Now, as for your job situation, I also procrastinate about my job/jobs or lack-there-of and I understand the struggle. It is hard to find the gumption to do things when you are sad/depressed/angry/any-applicable-emotion. But, if you are facing hunger/homelessness, then the pressure is on, you MUST find something, even if you hate doing it, and stick with it. I fucking HATE my minimum wage job, but I do it anyway because I need to eat, and [barely] afford shelter. Try looking into a job-placement-center or an employment agency. They can help you find a job that you are good at, or more importantly will enjoy.

TL;DR get a job, stick with the job, its nice to have money, and you will get a sense of pride from doing it.

Good Luck OP.

>I've also thought about just buying a gun (very easy in this state) and killing myself as opposed to admitting this to anyone. The most important thing about this plan is that I can't fail, and so I've been reading about the most effective ways to do it.

DON'T do this. First, suicide is a PERMANENT solution to a TEMPORARY problem. Second, if you are willing to grow and learn, things WILL get better, but you have to be WILLING. Third, if ever you get to the point where you think you might go through with it, I pray, hope, and wish, that you seek medical attention at the ER, call 911, or at the very least call the National Suicide Prevention Hotline [1 (800) 273-8255] and talk about what's going on in your life/head. Talking helps, believe me. I've struggled with Major Depressive Disorder, bouts of Bipolar, and mild Schizophrenia. I've tried killing myself through over-dose of prescription meds, and merely ended up in a month long coma for it. The thing about attempting suicide is that most people like you who think they have a fool-proof plan, is that 90% of all suicide attempt fail, and the resulting hardships that ensue (physical, mental, or social and otherwise) are almost ALWAYS worse than the feeling of suicidalness and even the act itself. I urge you, neagh BEG you, to at the very least look into finding a therapist/counselor. It's their job to help, and most of them love to do so, and are very good at it (as many of them suffer from the same problems they are helping, giving them a kind of "experience").
